applies_why: This judge text decides a clash involving the challenger's footed chain by citing the challenged sentence's own words, which is the kind of verse-by-verse weighing K-C governs.
quote: but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'never verse by verse.' Reading one: using the challenged sentence's own words to answer a footed chain is verse-by-verse weighing. Reading two: the judge only notes what the verse says and defers the actual answer to CR3 LINK 2, so it is not weighing verse by verse.
why: The judge resolves the clash by the challenged sentence's own words rather than by weighing the challenger's footed chain against the defender's chain by footing.
